references.text: This chapter gives the detailed laws about clean and unclean animals that Leviticus 20:25 refers to, including the distinction between clean and unclean animals, birds, and creeping things.
Summarizes the law of distinguishing between clean and unclean animals, which is the same principle affirmed in Leviticus 20:25.
Repeats the laws about clean and unclean animals that Israel must follow, in accordance with the command to distinguish between clean and unclean.
The preceding verse explains that God has set Israel apart from the nations, which is the basis for them also distinguishing between clean and unclean.
The following verse emphasizes Israel's holiness and that they are set apart to the Lord, which is the purpose of distinguishing between clean and unclean.
Ezekiel refers to the priests' responsibility to teach the people the difference between holy and common, clean and unclean.
Peter's vision where God declares all animals clean shows the New Testament fulfillment and abolition of the distinction between clean and unclean animals.
Peter recounts the vision about clean and unclean animals, which illustrates the transition from the Old to the New Covenant understanding of purity.
